main_strengths: Real tools fixed tool honesty: 0/20 items cite a backdrop value before get_macro_data (every early numeric hit is an episode id or the 4.5% benchmark), every L1/L2 Proof ref is a returned indicator or episode, all quoted values match the tool output, and 20/20 compute the real policy rate correctly.

Analog triage is the best so far: each item says which returned episodes fit and where they differ, sets aside off-topic ones (SVB for the peace deal, Argentina for the bank run, the house-price peak for PPI, BoJ YCC for the inversion) and switches analog when the data demand it (k0013 prefers EP-2009-03 to EP-2024-08-21 at the floor; k0006 weighs the 2023 no-recession inversion).

The Keynesian toolkit is sharper than in v2: the liquidity trap / zero bound is applied at policy rates of 0.5-1.0% (k0003, k0010, k0013, k0018) and explicitly ruled out at 2.5-5.5%; overheating is diagnosed and restraint prescribed (k0000, k0001, k0015, and k0016 with the batch's only bonds SHORT); wage deceleration is read as an AD contraction in deflation (k0013); reconstruction spending as a multiplier into idle capacity (k0014); a 3-day outage is sized through the circular flow (k0009).

Signals now weigh the distribution: 101/120 signal reasons cite more than one scenario, with correct probability sums (v2: 86/90 started from S1); only 5 cite S1 alone. Good news gets risk-on calls (k0001 SPR: equities LONG, gold SHORT; k0004 peace: equities and credit LONG, USD SHORT; k0007 and k0017 credit LONG) and small events get NEUTRALs (k0009, k0015).

Old artefacts are gone: 'no bp/pp' and 'newest information' 0/20, the 0.55/0.25/0.20 template 0/20, probabilities sum to 1.00 in 20/20, foreign events state their US channel, and real event-vs-backdrop contradictions are named (k0003, k0006, k0018).
main_problems: Bonds LONG 16/20 (NEUTRAL 3, SHORT 1) and credit SHORT 15/20. The event and data justify them in about 8 and 6 items (bank run, blockade risk, pandemic, deep contractions with restrictive real rates, deflation) and partly in 2 and 4. They are teacher defaults in 6 and 5. Bonds: k0003, k0009, k0012, k0015, k0017, k0019 (four with inflation-up mass >= 0.6; k0017 against its own 'bear-steepening' text). Credit: k0003, k0009, k0012, k0015, k0019 (k0012's own reason says spreads are unchanged in 0.60 of the mass; k0015 treats EM sovereign spreads as US HY; k0009 rests on a 0.05 tail). Bonds are LONG in 6 of the 8 positive-gap backdrops, 3 of them with no event reason (k0003, k0012, k0015). Gold is LONG 14/20, about 4 of them on the backdrop alone (k0009 admits no event case).

A new prompt echo replaces the old ones. Step 3's 'say so in one sentence and weigh the event more' yields 'I weigh the event more' in 18/20, mostly bolted onto manufactured tensions (k0009 weighs a 3-day Latin American outage against US core PCE; k0013 uses it where event and data agree; k0011 writes 'One sentence on the conflict:'). 'this school'/'the school's' appears in 16/20, the profile's 'A supply shock is a supply shock first' near-verbatim in 8/20 (k0008 and k0019 call it 'the school's rule'), and 'single print/set of values' in 5/20.

Calibration is templated in a new place: Confidence is 'moderate' in 20/20, and the modal scenario sits in 0.35-0.55 in 20/20 (0.42 or 0.45 in 12; 0.45/0.30/0.15/0.10 twice). So a 3-day outage (0.55), a frontier IMF request (0.52) and a pandemic (0.45) carry the same confidence, and tails are overweighted (an implemented blockade gets 0.65 in k0005 though the event only raises the risk).

Signal reasons mis-assign their own scenarios: k0002 oil ('only S4 offsets' though S1 is growth up), k0003 bonds (S4 is a no-change scenario), k0004 oil (growth-up S2 as 'lower demand'), k0007 gold (S2 'US unchanged' lowers real rates), k0008 bonds (stagflationary S3), k0012 USD/credit/oil (the reasons argue against the calls), k0016 gold (S3 is inflation down), and k0019 (the Proof says the easing-and-growth S1 drives the credit and oil shorts).

Proof discipline: 7/20 Proofs have 8-10 lines against the prompt's 4-7 (proof_problems accepts 4-10). L5 names a tail in k0001 (S3) and k0008 (S2); the Proof contradicts the weights in k0014 and the signals in k0017 and k0019; k0006 derives the real rate from the 10y.

Claims added beyond the tool text bring in errors: SVB's guarantee 'stopped the contagion within days' (k0000), 1994 as an inversion 'against high inflation' (k0006), Malaysia 'kept' its peg (k0010), AUD as part of DXY (k0007), food a smaller consumption share than energy (k0003), an invented 0.1pp miss (k0013), a US oil 'import bill' (k0001). EP-2009-03 and EP-2001-01 are recast against their own tool text (k0013, k0002).

Value and frame misreads: the curve is said to price easing when the 2y is at or above the policy rate (k0009, k0013); the pre-event backdrop is read as proof that the event has already spread to US credit (k0010); trends are read from single levels (k0002 '$41 reversal underway', k0005 'the 1990 configuration'); US rates and the US gap are applied to the UK and Australia (k0017, k0007); scenario tags mix foreign and US frames (k0010, k0015), with growth-down mass 1.00 in k0009 and k0015.

Concept stuffing has moved to the paradox of thrift: 11/20 use it (v2: 0/15) and about 6 misuse it (precautionary saving k0003, debt deflation k0013, shrinking real money balances k0017, firms hoarding cash k0005, foreign exit k0008, austerity k0015). Also: 'liquidity trap' at a 2.5% rate (k0007), the unemployment gap called the output gap (k0002), and an invented doctrine that 'the price-side gap measure is more reliable' (k0003).

Missed event-vs-data checks: 0.6% m/m (about 7.4% annualised) against 4.7% y/y is still read as an easing signal (k0002, the flaw from v1 and v2); PPI 4.0% is never compared with CPI 4.8% (k0016); a 75bp emergency hike is never compared with the steep hikes in its own analogs (k0008). Backdrops are still sometimes incoherent (unemployment 3.3% with 4.3% growth and 0.0% core PCE; a 0.42% 10y with 4.8% CPI; the 2y above the policy rate in -4% contractions), and 11/20 show negative GDP (7 at -3% or worse), which feeds the bonds LONG habit.
suggested_prompt_or_template_changes: teacher_messages_v4 step 3: replace 'If the data and the event point different ways ... say so in one sentence and weigh the event more' with 'Only if a returned value contradicts what the event states (e.g. the event says the curve inverted and the spread is positive), state the contradiction and which you rely on; otherwise say nothing about it.' Add META rejects for 'weigh the event', 'One sentence on', 'this school', 'the school's', 'school's rule' and 'single (print|set|point-in-time)', and have the batch report flag any 5-gram found in more than 25% of a school's items.

templates.toml, Keynesian diagnosis: rewrite the quotable 'A supply shock is a supply shock first; its demand effects come second' as 'separate the price effect of a supply shock from its income effect on demand, and say which dominates here'. In step 1, replace 'as this school reads it' with 'for growth and inflation'. Define the concepts the model misuses: paradox of thrift (higher desired saving lowers income, so total saving does not rise; not debt deflation, falling real balances or austerity), liquidity trap (policy rate at or near zero), and output gap vs unemployment gap (Okun, about 2:1).

Signals: require each reason to name what in this event moves the US asset (not the backdrop alone), and make 'NEUTRAL (conviction 1-2) - event too small or too remote to move US <asset>' the expected call for small foreign events. Validator flags: bonds LONG with inflation-up mass >= 0.6; credit or equities SHORT with growth-down mass < 0.5; a reason that cites a scenario whose growth/inflation tag points the other way (e.g. a growth-up scenario behind an oil or credit SHORT); conviction >= 4 resting on a scenario below 0.3. The existing 70% batch warning would fire here (bonds 80%, credit 75%, gold 70%) and should block a batch, not only report it.

Calibration: tie the confidence level and the modal probability to the event: 'a small, contained or well-precedented event: base case 0.6-0.85 and confidence high; an ambiguous or large event: spread the mass and confidence low'. Warn when one confidence level covers more than 70% of a school's items (20/20 'moderate' now) or the modal probability stays in 0.40-0.55 in more than 60%.

Scenarios: tag growth/inflation for the US/global economy against a no-event baseline, allow 'flat', and describe the foreign economy only in the causal chain. Add: 'no data for other economies were returned; never use US values for them' (k0007, k0017).

Proof: bring proof_problems in line with the prompt (4-7 steps, not 4-10), require exactly one L5 naming the modal scenario (a tail only when marked 'tail'), and check that the numbers in a Proof line come from the refs it cites (k0006).

Step 3 should check the event against the data: annualise m/m figures and compare them with the y/y rate; compare PPI with CPI; compare a stated move (bp or %) with the magnitudes in the returned episodes; read the 2y against the policy rate before saying what the market prices; and remember that the backdrop predates the event and cannot show its effects.

Episodes: 'describe a returned episode only as far as the tool text goes; add no later outcomes or mechanisms' (SVB, Malaysia, 1994, EP-2009-03). Define the asset referents in the prompt: US Treasuries, DXY (EUR, JPY, GBP, CAD, SEK, CHF; no AUD), US high yield (not EM sovereign spreads).

macro_snapshot: tie the 2y to the expected policy path (below the policy rate when growth is negative and unemployment is above 4.5%), keep the 10y within a band around inflation, keep core PCE consistent with the gap, and cut the share of negative-GDP draws (11/20 here, 7 at -3% or worse).

Before training, regenerate or repair the default-signal items (bonds: k0003, k0009, k0012, k0015, k0017, k0019; credit: k0003, k0009, k0012, k0015, k0019) and strip the 'I weigh the event more' and 'this school' sentences, ideally by regenerating after the prompt fix. The reasoning core (analog triage, real-rate and zero-bound checks, overheating diagnosis) is worth keeping.
